name: Hoover Dam
headline: height
description: Hoover Dam is a concrete arch-gravity dam in Black Canyon on the Colorado River, on the Arizona-Nevada state line. It was built between 1931 and 1936 and holds back Lake Mead. In cross-section it tapers like an axe head, from 660 ft thick at its base to 45 ft at the top, where a road crosses the crest.

facts.text: The dam itself contains three and one-quarter million cubic yards of concrete; the dam, powerplant and associated works together contain 4,360,000 cubic yards.
Hoover Dam weighs more than 6,600,000 tons.
The towers and ornaments on the parapet rise 40 feet above the crest.
The maximum water pressure at the base of the dam is 45,000 pounds per square foot.
As many as 20,000 vehicles a day drive across the 45 ft wide top of the dam between Nevada and Arizona.
The final bucket of concrete was placed in the main dam on May 29, 1935.

caveats: Reclamation pages give different concrete totals: 3.25 million cubic yards in the dam alone and 4,360,000 cubic yards including the powerplant and associated works (FAQ); 4,400,000 cubic yards for the dam, powerplant and associated structures (history and project-data pages); and '4 1/2 million cubic yards' (Kid Facts page).
The weight is given only as 'more than 6,600,000 tons', with no unit stated (probably short tons), so it is recorded as a fact rather than a measure.

Reclamation's project-data page confirms the headline dimensions independently of the FAQ and history pages: structural height 726.4 ft, crest length 1,244 ft, crest width 45 ft and base width 660 ft.
Reclamation describes the dam type in three ways: 'concrete arch-gravity' (FAQ), 'concrete gravity arch' (history page) and 'concrete thick arch' (project-data page).
